messages:
Anya: Quick update — ran 3 replay batches (prod traces) with the new deterministic sampler (preserves original cohort bucketing + seed) to try and keep KV-cache warmup shapes the same. Summary: functional parity fail on ~2% of traces, regression in p95 latency ~8ms on gpu-small kernels.

Mike L: can you paste the run cmd + config?

Anya: run command I used:
```
./replay --trace-dir s3://replay/prod/2026-03-10 --sampler deterministic --bucket-seed 42 --anon=true --preserve-cohorts=true --kernels=auto --batching=heuristic-v2
```
Config diff vs baseline: sampler=deterministic (new), preserve-cohorts=true (new), batching=heuristic-v2 (same as canary).

Samira: 2% parity fail sounds high. Do we have any diff logs showing functional divergence or just timing?

Anya: both. Failures are small token-delta mismatches (token ids differ) on ~260 traces out of 13k. Most of those traces hit the small-batch kernel fallback path (kernel id: aten_small_seq_v3). When I forced kernel=aten_large_seq (no fallback) for a subset, parity went to ~99.996%.

J. Gomez: interesting — so kernel fallback path appears nondeterministic vs primary kernel. Could be due to memcopy ordering between kernels or an RNG. Any signs in the replay logs?

Anya: Found this in the runtime logs around divergence points:
```
[2026-03-12 09:12:33] kernel-selector: chose aten_small_seq_v3 (reason: seq_len=12, batch=1)
[2026-03-12 09:12:33] kvcache: warmup hit=0.12 miss=0.88
[2026-03-12 09:12:33] runtime: fallback path executed, seed=unset
[2026-03-12 09:12:33] generation: token_idx=3 emitted=5021
```
Note the "seed=unset" line — looks like fallback path didn't set deterministic seed for some micro-kernel RNG used for attention masking.

Mike L: aha. We should add deterministic seeding to kernel entry for fallbacks. Also need to ensure kernel-to-kernel memcpy ordering is consistent. Samira — can you run a focused repro: same trace, force small kernel with seed=42 and with seed unset? Compare outputs.

Samira: on it. Quick question — the deterministic sampler preserves cohort bucketing which changes KV warmup distribution vs random sampling. Could that expose race-ish behavior by altering the timing?

Anya: exactly my hypothesis. Preserving cohorts changed the arrival order and batch boundaries, which increases instances that trigger small-batch kernel. We didn't catch this earlier because random sampling averaged those cases out.

playback-bot: replay-run 2319990000:3 batches completed — parity_fail=260/13000 (2.0%), p50=14ms p95=56ms p99=110ms, note=kernel-fallback-hotspot

J. Gomez: For immediate triage: 1) add deterministic seeding (quick patch) 2) run apples-to-apples with batching heuristics disabled (force fixed-batching) 3) instrument kernel memcpy order and sparse RNG usage 4) run deterministic sampler + synthetic mirrors (to reproduce outside prod traces).

Mike L: For (2) do we have a flag that disables heuristic batching? I remember an internal flag --batching=fixed-N. If not, add it so we can compare identical batch boundaries.

Anya: yes, --batching=fixed:16 works. I'll repro with fixed batches and deterministic kernel seed. Plan: run 13k traces with three configs: (A) baseline (random sampler + heuristic batching), (B) deterministic sampler + heuristic batching, (C) deterministic sampler + fixed batching + kernel-seed=42. Then compare token-level diffs and latency distributions.

Samira: timeline?

Anya: starting now; estimate 45m runtime per full run on the canary pool. Kicking off run (B) first, then A then C.

playback-bot: job 2319990000-B started on canary-pool-3 (eta ~45m)

J. Gomez: If (C) removes parity fails and regresses latency, then we know the issue is the small kernel path interaction with seeding. If parity remains, we need to look at quantization kernel diffs between small/large.

Samira: one more note — record per-token attention-mask state and KV-peek history for the failing traces. Small overhead but will help debug nondeterminism source.

Anya: added kv-peek trace logging for failing cohort, will attach results.

Mike L: great. Post results in this thread and include the diff command you use: e.g.,
```
./replay-diff --baseline s3://replay/results/A --candidate s3://replay/results/B --metrics tokens_different,p95_latency
```

Anya: will do. TL;DR: deterministic sampler surfaced a kernel-fallback nondeterminism tied to unset RNG seed and KV warmup changes. Immediate actions: patch kernel entry to set seed, run fixed-batch apples-to-apples, add memcpy/order instrumentation.

J. Gomez: thanks — assign to eng-runtime perf queue and add to the 48h gorilla list if we see >1% parity fail after the seed patch. :thumbsup:
